landmarks.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
landmarks.writeup: A grand royal palace in Seoul, originally built in 1395, symbolizing the Joseon Dynasty's heritage.

wiki.extract: Gyeongbokgung is a former royal palace in Seoul, South Korea. Established in 1395, it was the first royal palace of the Joseon dynasty, and is now one of the most significant tourist attractions in the country.

landmarks.name: N Seoul Tower
landmarks.writeup: A communication and observation tower offering panoramic views of Seoul.

wiki.extract: Namsan Seoul Tower, also known as the YTN Seoul Tower, Namsan Tower, Seoul Tower or N Seoul Tower, is a communication and observation tower located on the summit of Namsan in central Seoul, South Korea. The 236-metre-tall (774 ft) structure was the nation’s first tower servicing multiple TV and radio broadcasters, and is considered a landmark and symbol of the city.

landmarks.name: Jeju Island
landmarks.writeup: A volcanic island known for its unique natural beauty, including lava tubes and waterfalls.

wiki.extract: Jeju Island is South Korea's largest island, covering an area of 1,833.2 km2 (707.8 sq mi), which is 1.83% of the total area of the country. Alongside outlying islands, it is part of Jeju Province and makes up the majority of the province.

landmarks.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
landmarks.writeup: A traditional Korean village in Seoul with well-preserved hanok houses.

wiki.extract: Bukchon Hanok Village (Korean: 북촌한옥마을) is a residential neighborhood in Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea. It has many restored traditional Korean houses, called hanok. This has made it a popular tourist destination.

landmarks.name: DMZ (Demilitarized Zone)
landmarks.writeup: A buffer zone between North and South Korea, symbolizing the ongoing division of the peninsula.

wiki.extract: A demilitarized zone is an area in which treaties or agreements between states, military powers or contending groups forbid military installations, activities, or personnel. A DZ often lies along an established frontier or boundary between two or more military powers or alliances. A DZ may sometimes form a de facto international border, such as the Korean Demilitarized Zone. Other examples of demilitarized zones are a 14 km (8.7 mi) wide area between Iraq and Kuwait; Antarctica ; and outer space.

cultural_events.name: Chuseok
cultural_events.writeup: A major harvest festival where families honor ancestors and share traditional food.

wiki.extract: Chuseok, also known as Hangawi, is a major Korean mid-autumn harvest festival which occurs on the 15th day of the 8th month of the lunisolar calendar, on the full moon. In South Korea, the festival lasts for three days, including the days before and after the full moon. In North Korea, Chuseok is a single-day celebration on the full moon only.

cultural_events.name: Seollal
cultural_events.writeup: Korean Lunar New Year celebration involving ancestral rites, games, and traditional food.

wiki.extract: Seollal (Korean: 설날) is a Korean traditional festival and national holiday commemorating the first day of the Korean lunisolar calendar. It is one of the most important traditional holidays for ethnic Koreans, being celebrated in both North Korea and South Korea as well as Korean diaspora all around the world.

cultural_events.name: Boryeong Mud Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual festival featuring mud-based activities promoting health and fun.

wiki.extract: The Boryeong Mud Festival (Korean: 보령머드축제) is an annual festival which takes place during the summer on Daecheon Beach (대천해수욕장) near Boryeong, a town some 200 km south of Seoul, South Korea. The first Mud Festival was staged in 1998 and, by 2007, the festival attracted 2.2 million visitors to Boryeong.

cultural_events.name: Jinhae Cherry Blossom Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A spring festival celebrating cherry blossoms with parades and cultural performances.

wiki.extract: The Jinhae Gunhangje Festival (Korean: 진해군항제), also called Jinhae Cherry Blossom Festival, is a cherry blossom festival held in Jinhae District, Changwon, South Korea. It began in 1963 and is held annually in early April. It is also called Beotkkotjang because markets similar to five-day markets are formed on roads with cherry blossom trees.

cultural_events.name: Andong Mask Dance Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A cultural event showcasing traditional mask dances and folk performances.

wiki.extract: Andong is a city in South Korea, and the capital of North Gyeongsang Province. It is the largest city in the northern part of the province with a population of 167,821 as of October 2010. The Nakdong River flows through the city. Andong is a market centre for the surrounding agricultural areas.

food_writeup: South Korean cuisine is characterized by bold flavors and diverse dishes such as kimchi, bibimbap, bulgogi, and Korean barbecue, emphasizing fermented foods and a balance of spicy, sour, and savory tastes.
brief_history: South Korea was established in 1948 following the division of Korea after World War II. It experienced rapid economic growth and democratization in the late 20th century, becoming a leading global economy and vibrant democracy.

important_people.name: King Sejong the Great
important_people.description: Creator of the Korean alphabet Hangul

important_people.name: Park Chung-hee
important_people.description: Former President who led economic development

current_conflicts: Tense relations with North Korea persist, including occasional military provocations and unresolved political disputes stemming from the Korean War armistice.
